question: DAFgiving360 adviser-managed assets from its own audit: have the owner download DAFgiving360's FY2024 and FY2025 audited financial statements (www.dafgiving360.org returns 403 to robots.txt, so no automated fetch) and record any note splitting investments between pooled options and 'investment advisor' / professionally managed accounts, plus the line behind Form 990 Part IX line 11f
conclusion_affected: Adviser-managed share at DAFgiving360: now bracketed at 1.5% (hard floor) to 13% (if line 11f is all adviser fees at the 1% cap), with a 49% scenario at Fidelity's fee rate; the 77-78% figure is adviser-associated, not adviser-managed
rationale: Fidelity's audit Note 3 settles its share (46.9% of investments, June 2025). DAFgiving360 files line 11f of $61.4m (FY2025) and 101 contractors over $100k, but no public asset split; only its audit could give one

question: NPT UK / NPT Transatlantic accounts for FY2022-23 and FY2023-24 from the Charity Commission register (charities 1181128 and 1153376; the register page returned 'issue displaying this content' to a scripted fetch): confirm whether any NPT or NPT Transatlantic grant reached NPT UK before FY2024-25, and list FY2022-23 material grantees
conclusion_affected: Whether $0 of NPT's FY2023-24 foreign grants went to NPT UK (filed Schedule R line 1d 'No' both years; NPT UK absent from Transatlantic's FY2024 material list) and the size of the Transatlantic share (upper bound 18.2%)
rationale: Only the FY2024-25 accounts are linked from nptuk.org; FY2023 rests on the grantmaking report (£68m) and has no grantee list

question: Reconcile NPT's FY2025 Form 990 Schedule R Part V line 1d ('No' gift/grant to a related organisation) with NPT Transatlantic's £30.939m grant to NPT UK in the year to 30 June 2025 (Transatlantic is NPT's disregarded entity), and test whether the single $39.1m Europe line in FY2025 Schedule F Part II is that transfer
conclusion_affected: Netting of sponsor-to-affiliate flows in foreign-grant totals (cross-border analogue of DAF-to-DAF); FY2025 NPT foreign share
rationale: £30.939m at the FY2025 mean H.10 rate is $40.06m, 12.9% of NPT's FY2025 line 3; the largest FY2025 line is $39.1m in Europe labelled 'ENVIRONMENT, ANIMALS'. The size match is suggestive, not proof

question: Name the CIAP / adviser firms behind Fidelity Charitable's line 11f: Part VII-B shows only the five largest contractors (73 exceed $100k in FY2025). Collect firm-side disclosures (RIA brochures on firm websites, not sec.gov-hosted pages) that state they manage Fidelity Charitable CIAP or DAFgiving360 adviser accounts, and tag each as wirehouse, regional broker-dealer or independent RIA
conclusion_affected: Wirehouse share of adviser-managed DAF assets (UBS, Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo appear in Fidelity's top five; Graystone/Morgan Stanley at DAFgiving360; Edward Jones never appears)
rationale: Top-five contractor lists cover $25.8m of Fidelity's $84.3m FY2025 adviser fees and $7.2m of DAFgiving360's $61.4m; the rest of the firm mix is unseen

question: NPT segregated (adviser-managed) account assets: find NPT's full audited consolidated statements with notes for FY2024-FY2025 (only a two-page summary is on nptrust.org) and record any split of investments between pooled model portfolios and segregated accounts, plus the composition of the $116.3m asset management fees
conclusion_affected: NPT adviser-managed share (not estimable now); Wells Fargo-managed DAFs (Schedule L) and private-label partner programmes
rationale: NPT's line 11f ($93.8m FY2025, 22.5 bps of mean investments) mixes model-portfolio advisory fees with segregated-account adviser fees, so no fee-based bound is valid
